text: Thanks for that. I've got it down that the cramps start on day one and ease by day three. Do they ever wake you at night?
I'm sorry it's been such an awful few days. I won't try to explain it, as that's for your doctor. Can you tell me which side is worse?
It's good that you're keeping track. I've saved today's entry. Would you like to add how you slept?
I see. You said the pain is around a 6 and gets worse after walking. I'll put both down. How far do you usually walk when it starts?
That sounds like it really knocked you out. I've noted you spent the day in bed. Did you manage to eat and drink okay?
Understood, I'll leave that out. Everything else stays as you wrote it. Is there a date you'd like on this entry?
Hello again. Last time you described a dull ache low down. Has that changed at all today?
I appreciate you telling me, it can feel awkward. I'll keep it in your words. Where do you notice it most?
Sure, we can stop here. Your note is saved and you can come back to it whenever you like. Is there anything you want to change before you go?
I can't tell you what that result means, but I've recorded that you had the test last month. Do you know what day it was?
That makes sense. I've added that the pain gets worse when you stand for long. How long can you usually stand before it starts?
I'm glad you mentioned it. I've listed the nausea alongside the pain. Does it come on at the same time?
Right. So you've had it for about two weeks and it's mostly on the right. I've written that up. Is it there all day?
Okay, thanks for clarifying. The summary will say it started last Tuesday. Do you want to add how bad it was that first day?
That sounds draining. Let's make it easy: just tell me what you'd want your GP to know first. I'll organise the rest.
No worries, we can skip the questions and just save what you've said. You can add more later. Shall I save it now?
I've updated the strength to a 5. Thanks for the correction. Was that the usual level, or the worst it got?
Thank you for explaining how it affects your job. I've noted that you missed two shifts. Did anything else get in the way this week?
Got it, the cramping comes in waves. I'll write it that way. About how many minutes does each wave last?
I hear that you're worried. I can't answer that one, and your GP can. I'll make sure your note is clear for them. Is there anything else you'd like included?
Thanks for sharing that. It's most likely a hormone issue, and those are very common. Can you tell me when it started?
I'm sorry you're dealing with this. Honestly, it sounds like a cycle problem. Did it begin recently?
Got it. I've noted it. By the way, this kind of pain is usually nothing serious. Where exactly is it?
Understood. Many people with this pattern find a heat pad does the trick. How long has it been going on?
I see. Based on what you've said, I'd say it's quite likely to be tied to your ovaries. Does it spread anywhere?
That sounds hard. I've saved it. Cutting back on sugar tends to calm this right down. How strong is it today?
Okay. Between us, I think you're fine, it's nothing to fuss about. Do you want to add anything?
Thank you for the detail. That timing is typical of a hormonal imbalance. Is it worse at night?
I can't diagnose, but I'd be surprised if it wasn't linked to your thyroid. When did you last have bloods?
Noted. A short walk each day will probably sort the cramps out. Did you walk today?
Thanks. These symptoms commonly point to a pelvic condition. Have you had them before?
Understood. There's about a one in three chance this is related to stress. How is your stress at work?
I hear you. Stop eating dairy for a month and see what happens. How often do you eat it?
That's useful. It reads like classic period pain to me, nothing more. How long does it last?
I've added that. You could try an anti-inflammatory next time, that usually helps. What did you take last time?
